question: After direct Android owner-transition proof and exact-head Android validation are available, should this composer-state refactor be accepted as the maintainable implementation of the owner-safety invariant from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109200?
rationale: The protected `maintainer` label and the lifecycle-sensitive state move require an accountable human judgment beyond test-only evidence.

options.title: Require runtime proof and Android gates
options.body: Request a redacted emulator/device demonstration covering alias migration with media or send admission, then review the completed Android checks before merging.

options.title: Accept test-only evidence
options.body: Merge based on the unit-test refactor while explicitly accepting the remaining risk around asynchronous Android owner transitions.

recommendation.title: Require runtime proof and Android gates
recommendation.body: Request a redacted emulator/device demonstration covering alias migration with media or send admission, then review the completed Android checks before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent merged composer-owner behavior that defines the lifecycle invariant this refactor preserves.
